content.value_statement: Complex systems often fail because boundaries, models, and tradeoffs are unclear. This skill guides discovery, modeling, architecture decisions, and TypeScript scaffolding.
actual_capabilities: Guides architecture sessions through discovery, modeling, boundaries, and scaffolding phases.
Uses Clean Architecture and Hexagonal Architecture references to explain tradeoffs.
Helps define domain entities, value objects, ports, adapters, and bounded contexts.
Produces ADR-style decision records with context, decisions, consequences, and risks.
Provides TypeScript templates for repositories, controllers, use cases, and value objects.
Creates Mermaid-style domain models and boundary maps when requested.
limitations: It does not choose architecture decisions without user input.
It does not validate generated scaffolds against a running build by itself.
It focuses on TypeScript examples and may need adaptation for other languages.
It does not replace security, performance, or compliance review for production systems.

use_cases.title: Plan a new service architecture
use_cases.description: Turn a product idea into actors, domain concepts, boundaries, and initial architecture decisions.

use_cases.title: Refactor toward ports and adapters
use_cases.description: Identify dependencies that cross boundaries and design interfaces for safer replacement.

use_cases.title: Document architecture decisions
use_cases.description: Create ADRs that explain context, selected options, rejected options, and follow-up risks.

prompt_templates.title: Start architecture discovery
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: clarify the problem before choosing a structure.
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to architect a new system for [business problem]. Guide me through discovery questions first.

prompt_templates.title: Model the domain
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: identify entities, value objects, and domain events.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me model the domain for [system]. Identify entities, value objects, events, and important invariants.

prompt_templates.title: Define ports and adapters
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: separate core logic from databases, APIs, and interfaces.
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these use cases and external systems, define inbound ports, outbound ports, adapters, and dependency direction.

prompt_templates.title: Generate scaffold and ADR
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: create implementation structure after decisions are clear.
prompt_templates.prompt: Using our approved architecture decisions, generate a TypeScript hexagonal scaffold plan and an ADR draft.

output_examples.input: I need to design an order management service.
output: Discovery questions about actors, failure modes, data ownership, and success measures.
A domain model with orders, customers, payments, inventory, and domain events.
A boundary map showing controllers, use cases, repositories, gateways, and adapters.

output_examples.input: Help me refactor a service that mixes controllers, SQL, and business rules.
output: A diagnosis of boundary problems and dependency direction issues.
Suggested ports for persistence, payments, notifications, and external services.
A migration path that extracts one use case before broad restructuring.

output_examples.input: Create an ADR for choosing Hexagonal Architecture.
output: A concise context section that names current coupling and testing problems.
A decision section that explains ports, adapters, and dependency rules.
Consequences that list benefits, tradeoffs, risks, and review checkpoints.

best_practices: Complete discovery and modeling before asking for a scaffold.
Keep business rules in the domain or use case layer.
Review each ADR with the team before implementation begins.
anti_patterns: Do not use the scaffold before naming the core domain concepts.
Do not let adapters contain business decisions that belong in the core.
Do not treat generated templates as production code without review and tests.

faq.question: Does this skill write complete production services?
faq.answer: No. It creates architecture guidance, templates, and scaffold plans that need implementation and testing.

faq.question: Which architecture styles does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on Clean Architecture, Hexagonal Architecture, ports and adapters, and domain modeling.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it support languages beyond TypeScript?
faq.answer: The concepts are general, but the included scaffolds and examples are TypeScript-oriented.

faq.question: When should I start with scaffolding?
faq.answer: Start scaffolding after the problem, domain model, boundaries, and core architecture decisions are clear.

faq.question: Can it help with an existing system?
faq.answer: Yes. It can analyze structure, identify boundary issues, and suggest incremental refactoring steps.
